_meta.indication: Treatment of seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) or Dravet syndrome (DS) in patients 2 years of age and older

pivotal_trials.design: 14-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; 1:1:1 to CBD 10 mg/kg/day, CBD 20 mg/kg/day, or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, ages 2-55, with ≥2 drop seizures per week on ≥1 concomitant AED
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage change from baseline in drop seizure frequency (average per 28 days) during the 14-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.n: 225 patients (76 at 20 mg/kg/day, 73 at 10 mg/kg/day, 76 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Median percentage change in drop seizure frequency -41.9% (20 mg/kg/day) and -37.2% (10 mg/kg/day) vs -17.2% placebo; both statistically significant vs placebo (p=0.0047 and p=0.0016)

pivotal_trials.design: 14-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; 1:1 to CBD 20 mg/kg/day or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (same criteria as Study 1414)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from baseline in drop seizure frequency (average per 28 days) during the treatment period
pivotal_trials.result: Median percentage change in drop seizure frequency -43.9% (CBD) vs -21.8% placebo; statistically significant (p=0.0135)

pivotal_trials.design: 14-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; 1:1 to CBD 20 mg/kg/day or placebo
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from baseline in total convulsive seizure frequency during the treatment period
pivotal_trials.result: Median percentage change in convulsive seizure frequency -38.9% (CBD) vs -13.3% placebo; statistically significant (p=0.0123)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and greater than placebo): somnolence, decreased appetite, diarrhea, transaminase elevations, fatigue/malaise/asthenia, rash, insomnia, and infections. Dose-related hepatocellular injury: ALT >3x ULN in 13% of EPIDIOLEX vs 1% placebo. Somnolence/sedation 32% vs 11% placebo.
target_moa: The precise mechanism of the anticonvulsant effect is unknown; cannabidiol does not appear to act through cannabinoid receptors
modality: Small molecule (cannabinoid derived from Cannabis sativa)

advisory_committee.vote: PCNS Advisory Committee (April 19, 2018) voted unanimously 13 Yes, 0 No that the benefit-risk profile was favorable
